purpose: This medicine is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, hair, and nails — such as ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, and fungal nail infections. It works best for infections that have not responded to creams or ointments alone. You will need to take it by mouth for several weeks or even months depending on where the infection is.
how_it_works: Griseofulvin works by getting into your skin, hair, and nails through your bloodstream and making it impossible for the fungus to grow and spread. It basically stops the fungus from making new cells. Over time, as your body grows new healthy skin, hair, or nails, the infection clears up and goes away.
common_side_effects: Headache (very common, especially early on), upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, skin rash or sensitivity to sunlight, dizziness, and trouble sleeping. Most of these are mild and often go away as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can harm an unborn baby. Men should also avoid fathering a child during and for 6 months after treatment. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication as it can cause flushing and a fast heartbeat. This drug can make birth control pills less effective, so use a backup method. It may also make you more sensitive to sunlight, so wear sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors.
typical_dosing: Adults typically take 375 mg once daily or in divided doses with a fatty meal (like peanut butter or whole milk) to help the medicine absorb better. The dose and length of treatment depend on which part of the body is infected — skin infections may need 2-4 weeks, scalp infections up to 4-6 weeks, and nail infections can take 4-6 months or longer. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
